notes.title: Sawera hone par Phela khyal ho tum
notes.content:

dophere mein jo khud se puchta hu, wo pyara
sawal ho tum.
Sham dhalte-dhalte mein tumhari yadoo

Aur dua karta hu
Jishe sirf mein pad saku wo kitab ban jao
Jo sirf mujhe ae wo khwab ban jao
Jispe sirf Mera adhikar ho wo gulab ban jao
Mehfil mein baat kar saku wo baat ban jao
Jo sirf mere sang gujre wo raat ban jao
Aur Jo sirf mujhe chadhe wo jamh ban jao
Ek khwaish hai ki
Mere Chote se dil ke mehman ban jao
Jishe zindagi bhar karu wo kaam ban jao
Sach kahu, tho meri jaan ban jao!

notes.title: For a long time now, every meeting with
notes.content:
For a long time now, every meeting with
another human being has been a
collision. I feel too much, sense too
much, am exhausted by the
reverberations after even the simplest
conversation. But the deep collision is
and has been with my unregenerate,
tormenting, and tormented self. I have
written every poem, evezy novel, for the
same purpose-to find out what I think, to
know where I stand. I am unable to
become what I see. I feel like an
inadequate machine, a machine that
breaks down at crucial moments, grinds
to a dreadful halt, "won't go," or, even
woise,explodes in some innocent
person's face.

night a negotiation with ghosts.

notes.title: Do you know why I shrink when a crowd
notes.content:
Do you know why I shrink when a crowd
forms? Why I give up my seat for
someone else to sit? Why I order the
cheapest thing on the menu when
someone else is paying? Why I give
away the last piece of the cookie even
when I wanted it the most? ltls because
I've spent my whole life trying to take up
less space. Because somewhere along
the way i convinced myself that existing
too loudly was a burden. And so, I
learned to fade to exist quietly, gently,
almost invisibly...

notes.title: When morning breaks, you are my very first
notes.content:
When morning breaks, you are my very first
thought.
By afternoon, you become the tender question
I quietly ask myself.
As evening slowly settles,
I lose myself in memories of you,
And in the dreams of the night,
I become wholly yours.
And so I prayyy,
Become the book only I am allowed to read.
Become the dream that comes only to me.
Become the rose that belongs to no one but my
hands.
Become the conversation I can share in a
crowded room.
Become the night that passes only beside me.
Become the wine that intoxicates only my soul.
I hold one wish close to my heart—
Become a guest in my small, fragile heart.
Become the purpose I choose for a lifetime.
And if I speak the truth...
Become my life itself.

notes.title: Datee
notes.content:
Datee
I have a date with Jane today.
All is ready. Morning waits.
We walk together to the church,
quiet steps, shared silence.
Afterward, coffee warms our hands,
cake is broken, sweet and soft
in a small café.
We wander through the park,
leaves listening to our thoughts.
Then the aquarium—
dolphins turning joy into water,
penguins, her favorites,
moving like gentle laughter.
After lunch, we rest.
Time loosens its grip.
"So what did we do this morning?"
we ask, smiling,
and speak of it again and again
until memory blurs,
until remembering feels unnecessary.
Sleep finds us.
And the night holds us
back at the church,
where the day began.

notes.title: And when death finally finds me, I hope it
notes.content:
And when death finally finds me, I hope it
doesn't come as a stranger. I hope it leans
close and whispers, "Come now... the fight is
over."
I hope it takes my hand gently,
like an old friend who knows my name, who
understands why my bones are tired and my
heart has learned to ache quietly.
I hope it says, "You've carried more than your
share. You don't have to be strong anymore.
Let me hold this weight for you."
I hope it promises me a place where the noise
cannot follow, where nothing asks and nothing
hurts.
A place where I am not broken, only finally still.
A place where it whispers, softly, "Here, there is
quiet. Here... you may rest."

notes.title: started noticing how often I look at something and
notes.content:
started noticing how often I look at something and
think, one day, when I'm better, 11m going to miss
some of the beautiful things I can't see right now
because I'm hurting too much. Like when I'm making
coffee and it's raining outside and I have a book in
mind which reads like it could be my new favourite, or
when I'm cuddling my blankets, lights turned off,
music in the background, and I'm half-listening, half-
thinking about when I was in third grade and my dad
read me a funny book about numbers to make me like
math. It's infuriating, really: to be nostalgic for the
present tense, to feel the loss of what hasn't even left
yet, because I don t feel alive enough to be happy
with it yet. I'm trying to learn how to stay in a moment
without mentally packing it away for later, for when
I'm better. or happier. The other day I went for a walk
and saw the sky looking like God's canvas of pink and
orange and blue, and it almost made me believe
again. I reached for my phone, thought "this'll look
nice later," but I let it stay unphotographed. Maybe
not every beautiful thing needs to be rescued fic time.
Some things deserve to disappear right on schedule.
And I deserve to
be happy with it right now. I don't deserve to store it
away for a hypothetical future in which I'm smiling.
Sometimes I think that's what growing up really is -
slowly becoming tware of how temporary everything
is, and trying to love it anyway.
Maybe years from now I'll look back on this exact
thought, and miss or ever. be proud of this version of
myself- the one

notes.title: As a final act of love I'll let you leave without ever
notes.content:
As a final act of love I'll let you leave without ever
knowing how bad it hurts. I'll memorize the sound of
the door closing and pretend it didn't echo through
my ribs. I'll keep answering "I'm fine" with a throat full
of glass because you don't need to carry my grief too.
You get to start over with clean hands. I'll stay here
with the stain of you on everything, learning how to
breathe around the hollow you carved out. If loving
you means bleeding quietly so you can heal, then I'll
do it. God. I'll do it.
